items.note: Story 1: 'In January 1925 they petitioned', tied to the 1924 rise from 3.61 to 3.80 with nothing changed on the farms.
Alonzo Frick chairman of a board of three; sat 17 March at Ashlin, twice in April in the station's weigh room, closing 4 May 1925 — three sessions, two at the station.
'Three explanations were argued — water (Vose), cream theft (Teague), wet hay (the 1908 report read in) — and none accepted.'

'Before it were four books only': test book, receiving book, Brant's weigh book, Strawn's 1923 notebook (named as Exhibit 4). Core fact of the item present; the gloss about the notebook holding the answer is interpretive context.
Dismissed 30 April 1925 by letter; 4 May award of $3,800 'without admission', charged to the station account, board finding 'no cause established'.

Half only. Story 2 gives '$3,800 award had been a fifth of it [$19,000]', but nowhere in Section A does the sheet identify the account the award was charged to with the account the 'station gain' had been accumulating in since 1898. 'Charged to the station account' already carries A7.5 and cannot be scored twice.
Ivy Keddie, born 1931, Ansel's granddaughter (Duncan's daughter), graduate student in dairy husbandry at the State Agricultural College, Farland, under Professor Leland Vaught.
'She then laid side by side what nobody had': test book, Roy's weigh book, Rosalie's Alder Corners table, Strawn's 1923 volume, the annual ledgers.
February 1958, up the ladder into the loft over the station intake room; crate found; nine pipettes unbroken.
9 March 1958 against a calibrated burette: 16.70-16.74, mean 16.72 against 17.6 marked, short 0.88 c.c., 95 hundredths of the mark.

'3.61 / 0.95 = 3.80; the gap of 0.19 was one-twentieth of the true test' — 95 percent of true, 0.19 short, and not a constant. Bounds given in Story 1 (12 June 1923, 3.61 every year since 1898, twenty-six years).

All four required elements inside Section A: 40,000,000 lb over twenty-five years at 1,600,000 a year (Story 1), 76,000 lb, $19,000 at 25 cents, and the identity with the ledgers' 'station gain' entries summed 1898-1922 (Story 2).
Bulletin No. 471, October 1958, quoted as clearing him; 'Thirty-five years from glass to cause, thirty-three from dismissal' and the diary's 'twenty-four years after his death'.

Cap reached several times over. Clean find+resolve+method on the 1924 average (3.80 against 3.90/3.85, by arithmetic), the weigh book's 1 Jan 1897 start (exhibit list), Orra's 1866 birth (arithmetic), Strawn's 1907 start (his own entry), the crate in the loft (finder's account against Nym's catalogue), Nym's transposed keepers, the sixteen-season overlap (the factory's table), Selby's 1913 start, and the 1908 committee against the 1925 board.

Part B is a dedicated near-tie list of 20 pairs, each naming the two carriers and the breaker: NT-1 (16.27, Vaught+Chronicle, broken by Ivy's nine readings and the 0.95 ratio), NT-11 (12 July, Selby+Rundle, broken by the 28 June order), NT-14 ($77.39, Junia+Chronicle, broken by summing Junia's own facsimile), NT-19 (first cousin once removed, Vira+Cleve, broken by the pedigree), and more. Cap reached.

Item 53: 'Accident, a reground mold (Junia) vs knowing fraud (Chronicle) -> not provable', with what is established (the uniformity of the nine pipettes; the Chronicle's is inference from silence; the 1931 works fire noted in Part C). Correct abstention where the question is put; the sheet's contrary assertions elsewhere are charged as a deduction, not against this item.
Item 5 settles it: 'Source of the 1911 measure ... -> Larrow Green [tester's own book; Roy's fails on Strawn's June 1911 entry]'. A headline verdict, not an abstention.
Item 58: Article VII's date 1891/1892/1893 '-> cannot be settled; the pamphlet is undated and the 1889-92 minute book lost'.

Part C lists sixteen on-the-page self-refutations, including Junia's $77.93 facsimile against her own '$77.39' and her 'nothing into Ordell before 1900' against an 1897 invoice, Duncan's 1868 against 'eighty-two in 1948', Grigg's 'whole of 1908' against his own three-month report, and Keddie's Ashlin creamery against his own first leaf.

Names the 1897 Ammon pipettes at 16.72 against 17.6, derives 0.95 and 0.19 as five percent of 3.80 (proportional, scaling with fat, flat across seasons), and bounds both ends: 1896 borrowed glass at 3.80, 1898 at 3.61; condemned 12 June 1923, 1924 back at 3.80, nothing on the farms changed.

Watering named to Selby Vose (1919 circular, 1926 address) and Hobart Sill, defeated by Strawn's lactometer at every visit, the Alder Corners cheese, the flatness of the gap, the 1911 weeks, and the ledger surplus.

Theft named to Teague (and Rundle, Vira, Cleve's father) and defeated by the station-gain line — stolen cream reaches the Green light and it arrived heavy for twenty-five years — plus the 1911 interval and the 1923-24 rise under the same tester.

Bog hay named to Grigg's 1908 committee and Dr. Kepp, defeated by Bulletin 214's 'not more than five hundredths in winter, and nothing on summer pasture' against a flat 0.19, by Alder Corners, by 1911, and by the error scaling with fat.

ABSTENTION A07 failed. Opens with a headline verdict — 'Did the 1925 board examine the condemned glassware? No.' — and closes 'never looked at, or asked for, the glass itself'. Later qualification does not undo a verdict sentence.

ABSTENTION A05 correct. Verdict sentence is 'whether he privately blamed the glass or the patrons cannot be determined', with the 1911 question mark, his 'I cannot tell you why the figures are what they are', and Frick against Duncan as single uncorroborated recollections. Leaning while declining is a correct abstention.
Over the cap. 151 words counting alphanumeric tokens only (155 raw whitespace tokens). The limit is 150.
Seven series: test book, weigh book, ledgers, cheese-factory book, inspector's notebook, invoice, and the 1958 measurement (plus the committee report and bulletin).
Clean. 'Water, theft, and wet hay were blamed' — none adopted; figures are 16.72, 17.6, 3.61, 3.80, one part in twenty. No wrong headline number.
Four of six elements, both ends covered: one part in twenty, 1 May 1897 onset, condemned 1923, measured 1958. Missing: 76,000 lb / $19,000, and Ivy is 'his granddaughter' rather than named.

deductions.reason: Corruption: F1.2 asserts Strawn's lactometer visits as running '1908-1936', the planted 1908 circuit start, in the sheet's own voice and unhedged — even though the sheet correctly resolves 1907 at E1 item 24 and Part B item 17. The deduction follows the sheet wherever the value is asserted.

Gullibility A04: the sheet asserts the accident pole outside E-c. Section A Story 2 — 'an accusation ... that Junia Ammon's 1949 history had already answered: a reground mold, an accident nobody caught' — and F1 — 'pipettes from a lot whose mold had been reground'. Deduction applies even though the E-c item itself was earned.
Gullibility A06: E1 item 5 names the lender of the 1911 measure — 'Larrow Green by cream wagon' — as a settled resolution with a method. The sources cannot settle it.
Gullibility A07: F1 answers 'Did the 1925 board examine the condemned glassware?' with a one-word headline verdict, 'No.'
